items.claim: Every Hebrew form, the ketiv/qere disclosure and all five parashah citations hold against the bytes and the WLC inventories, and no byte-true device crosses either seam undisclosed.
items.evidence: The opening command collates at byte tier against MT 10:17 and is second-person feminine on the pointed bytes themselves, אִסְפִּ֥י מֵאֶ֖רֶץ כִּנְעָתֵ֑ךְ (imperative in final -i governing the 2fs suffix -ekh), so the addressee identification does not rest on the English. The ketiv/qere disclosure is exact: the WLC inventory records one note at MT 10:17 and both forms stand in the source bytes, ketiv ישבתי (unpointed, skeleton grade) beside qere יֹשֶׁ֖בֶת (byte), a feminine participle agreeing with that command. The speech formula at MT 10:18 is byte-true and subordinated by ki exactly as argued, כִּֽי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה, and the mouth is Yahweh's own rather than quoted or reported speech; ק֤וֹל שְׁמוּעָה֙ is byte-true at MT 10:22. The negative claim about the internal turns survives the bytes: within this chapter that formula stands only at MT 10:2 and MT 10:18 (skeleton sweep: 152 verses book-wide for koh amar YHWH, 50 of them with tsevaot), and neither witness renders any imperative or names any new addressee across MT 10:19-22, while the first-person turn at MT 10:19 is disclosed rather than suppressed. All five mark citations match the inventory as setumah at MT 10:16, 10:17, 10:18, 10:21 and 10:22, petuchah is never conflated with setumah, and in-span disclosure is complete. The doxology twin closes at MT 10:16, so nothing byte-true crosses the opening seam. medium_low with the frontier flag set is calibrated to the voice turn the unit itself holds open.

items.claim: The unqualified statement that nothing before this verse addresses Yahweh in the second person is refuted by the bytes of MT 10:6-7, seventeen verses earlier in the same chapter.
items.evidence: MT 10:6 reads כָּמ֖וֹךָ יְהוָ֑ה גָּד֥וֹל אַתָּ֛ה (byte) and carries שִׁמְךָ֖ (byte); MT 10:7 opens מִ֣י לֹ֤א יִֽרָאֲךָ֙ (byte). Second-person masculine suffixes, the independent pronoun and a 2ms verbal object run through both verses, and both witnesses render them as direct address to Yahweh rather than as description of him, so the stated discriminator for the opening seam is false as written. The exclusivity is also unsourced, asserted without naming a swept object or citing a sweep count. The cut at MT 10:22|10:23 nonetheless survives on independent grounds the unit already holds, the setumah at MT 10:22 and the turn into petition addressed to Yahweh at MT 10:23-24, יָדַ֣עְתִּי and יַסְּרֵ֥נִי (both byte), so the defect lies in the warrant rather than in the boundary. The petuchah at MT 10:25 and the setumah at MT 10:22 are correctly typed and not conflated, and in-span mark disclosure is complete.

items.claim: The opening header is byte-perfect, but two byte-true catchwords cross this unit's closing seam undisclosed, and confidence is set at high with the frontier flag unset.
items.evidence: Frame ownership checks out completely: MT 11:1 is byte-identical to MT 7:1 across the whole verse, the preposition is אֶֽל and not the ayin-lamed variant that would put it outside the superscription family, and the header core sweeps to exactly eleven verses (skeleton sweep: 11 verses), so this is a confirmed member of that family and no shape is blended. The closing edge is the problem. The clause שִׁמְע֕וּ אֶת דִּבְרֵ֖י הַבְּרִ֣ית הַזֹּ֑את stands at MT 11:2 inside this span and recurs at MT 11:6, beyond the cut, as שִׁמְע֗וּ אֶת דִּבְרֵי֙ הַבְּרִ֣ית הַזֹּ֔את -- skeleton-identical, not byte-identical -- and those are the only two verses in the book carrying it (skeleton sweep: 2 verses). The summons שִׁמְע֤וּ בְקוֹלִי֙ at MT 11:4 likewise recurs beyond the cut at MT 11:7 as שִׁמְע֖וּ בְּקוֹלִֽי, again skeleton-identical and not byte-identical (skeleton sweep: 4 verses). Both are byte-true devices straddling this unit's own seam, neither is disclosed anywhere in the unit, and unaddressed they argue that the commission runs on through MT 11:8. The recurrence claim to MT 7:1 also carries no tier label, precisely where one is owed, since the two verses are byte-identical. High confidence with the frontier flag unset is not calibrated to an undisclosed straddling pair on the closing edge. The petuchah at MT 10:25 and the setumah at MT 11:5 are correctly typed and correctly held as corroboration rather than as drivers.

items.claim: The closing verse is characterised as carrying a covenant curse although the curse lexeme reaches MT 11:3 and not MT 11:8 (skeleton sweep: 5 verses book-wide), and the closing-seam formula is asserted as the same form without a splice or a tier although the two forms differ in the pointed bytes.
items.evidence: The closing characterization places the covenant curse at MT 11:8, but that verse reads אֶֽת כָּל דִּבְרֵ֧י הַבְּרִית הַזֹּ֛את (byte), the words of the covenant, with no curse lexeme anywhere in it. The curse word אָר֣וּר sweeps to five verses book-wide (skeleton sweep: 5 verses) and within this chapter stands only at MT 11:3, outside this span and uncited. What MT 11:8 actually carries is the covenant-words catchword binding MT 11:2, 11:3, 11:6 and 11:8 (skeleton sweep: 5 verses, four of them in this chapter), which crosses this unit's opening seam and is likewise undisclosed. Separately, the closing-edge argument rests on the assertion that MT 11:9 opens with the same introduction again, with no Hebrew spliced for that verse and no tier named: the two are skeleton-identical but not byte-identical, MT 11:6 reading וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י against the pausal MT 11:9 וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י (skeleton sweep: 13 verses). The cut is independently corroborated by the setumah at MT 11:8, correctly typed and correctly held as corroboration, so the boundary itself stands.

items.claim: The discriminator separating this unit from what precedes is contradicted by this unit's own second verse, and the speech formula on which its rejected alternative turns is left unspliced.
items.evidence: The stated ground is that MT 11:9 turns to the present generation's conspiracy rather than to the fathers' history just recalled. MT 11:10, inside this span, reads עַל עֲוֺנֹ֨ת אֲבוֹתָ֜ם הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֗ים and closes אֶת אֲבוֹתָֽם (both byte): the forefathers named twice in one verse, with the broken covenant tied to them, so the fathers' history is exactly what this span carries forward and the contrast does not survive the bytes. The same contrast is reused as the rejected alternative, so both the boundary argument and the alternative rest on it. Second, the speech formula at MT 11:11 is the pivot on which a fresh cut is refused, yet no Hebrew form is quoted for it anywhere in the unit; its bytes read לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה, and it is the one frame-form claim here left unspliced, while the introduction at MT 11:9 cited in the same unit is spliced and tiered. The mouth is named as divine, and the seam is independently corroborated by the setumah at MT 11:8, with the setumah citations at MT 11:10 and MT 11:13 correctly typed and in-span disclosure complete, so the boundary holds while its stated warrant does not.

items.claim: The link holding verses 16 and 17 together is mis-described as a planting in verse 16, although the planting participle occurs at MT 11:17 (skeleton sweep: 1 verse in the book), and the recorded signal labels a prohibition an imperative.
items.evidence: The unit argues that MT 11:17 names the same tree just planted in MT 11:16. The planting participle הַנּוֹטֵ֣עַ occurs in exactly one verse in the whole book, MT 11:17 (skeleton sweep: 1 verse), and MT 11:16 carries no form of that root at all, its verb being קָרָ֥א יְהוָ֖ה שְׁמֵ֑ךְ (byte). The link the argument is reaching for is real, but it is the second-person feminine chain: שְׁמֵ֑ךְ at MT 11:16 picked up by הַנּוֹטֵ֣עַ אוֹתָ֔ךְ and עָלַ֖יִךְ at MT 11:17 (all byte), which the unit's own splice displays while the prose relocates the planting to the wrong verse. The feminine-addressee reading is otherwise byte-sound across MT 11:15-17. Separately, the recorded signal calls the opening a discourse imperative while the prose correctly calls it a prohibition: אַל תִּתְפַּלֵּל֙ (byte) is the negative particle with a prefix-conjugation form, not an imperative, and both witnesses render it as a prohibition; form-class labels are byte-checkable claims held to the same discipline as digits. The four-verse hold, the divine-title reading at MT 11:17 and all three setumah citations at MT 11:13, 11:14 and 11:17 are correct and correctly typed.

items.claim: The statement that nothing before this verse is cast in this voice is refuted by the first-person chain closing MT 11:5, thirteen verses earlier, and again by MT 10:19-24.
items.evidence: MT 11:5 closes וָאַ֥עַן וָאֹמַ֖ר אָמֵ֥ן יְהוָֽה (byte), a first-person common singular wayyiqtol chain in which the prophet reports answering, thirteen verses before the verse said to introduce that voice, and both witnesses render it as his own first-person speech. Earlier still MT 10:19 carries וַאֲנִ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי (byte) with the first-person suffixes running on through MT 10:20, and MT 10:23-24 are first-person petition, יָדַ֣עְתִּי and יַסְּרֵ֥נִי (both byte). The claim carries no digit-bearing sweep and names no swept object, so an exclusivity is asserted where the bytes contest it three times over within the two adjacent chapters. Secondarily, the closing claim that the prayer is addressed to Yahweh of Armies rests on MT 11:20, whose וַֽיהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ is byte-true but is left unspliced, so the divine-title signal recorded for this unit has no quoted form behind it. The seam at MT 11:17|11:18 is independently supported by the setumah at MT 11:17 and by the genuine turn into first-person narration, and the setumah at MT 11:20 is correctly typed, so the boundary holds.

items.claim: The English set against the second formula renders a different clause of the verse than the spliced form, and the two therefore-clauses are treated as one object although they are distinct census objects.
items.evidence: The splice for MT 11:22 is לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת and it does collate at byte tier, but the English paired with it in the same breath renders הַבַּֽחוּרִים֙ יָמֻ֣תוּ בַחֶ֔רֶב instead, a later clause of the same verse; the rendering of the spliced formula itself is the therefore-Yahweh-of-Armies-says clause the pairing skips, so gloss extent and splice extent do not match and the byte-verified form is presented as saying something it does not say. The count objects are blended as well: MT 11:21 carries לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ without tsevaot (skeleton sweep: 152 verses) while MT 11:22 carries לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת, the tsevaot-expanded formula and a separate object (skeleton sweep: 50 verses). Describing the second as a further therefore-thus-says-Yahweh clause naming the same speaker leaves the tsevaot expansion unnamed, and that expansion is the byte fact that would actually carry the intensification reading argued here. Both clauses are byte-true at their cited refs, the mouth is named as Yahweh's in both and is neither quoted nor reported speech, and the setumah citations at MT 11:20, 11:21 and 11:23 match the inventory and are correctly typed, so the one-unit conclusion stands.
